_comment: Detectability thresholds. The robust signals are SHAPE/ratio based (coefficient of variation, timer-ratio stability, capability presence), not absolute cycle counts, which depend on CPU frequency and microarchitecture. Absolute cycle bounds are given only as coarse sanity rails. Sources: Intel SDM Vol.3; AMD PPR; and measured ranges. Treat these as advisory — tune per host.

rdtsc_cpuid_rdtsc.vm_like_if: median > 800 (primary); cv < 0.08 only annotates how obvious
rdtsc_cpuid_rdtsc.comment: The analyzer judges this by the MEDIAN: cpuid on bare metal is a few hundred cycles, so median > 800 means a VM-exit regardless of variance. Low cv just says the exit is steady/obvious. This is a KNOWN-HARD case: on vanilla KVM the VM-exit cannot be hidden and reads VM-like. VM_EXIT_JITTER raises cv (defeats a naive low-variance detector) but leaves the median high, so this stays KNOWN — see jitter_report.py.

cache_latency._source: Intel SDM Vol.3B Table B-6, AMD PPR
cache_latency.comment: Under EPT/NPT a guest is close to native; mainly characterizes the host. Flags only grossly wrong values (e.g. L1 > 8 cyc).

tsc_sync.comment: Cross-core |offset| should be small and stable. Large/negative offsets or big spread indicate non-invariant or trapped TSC.

hpet_tsc_ratio.comment: TSC-per-ns ratio must be stable (cv < 0.2%). Drift suggests rescaled/trapped TSC.

pmu_check.comment: A real CPU exposes an architectural PMU. version 0 / 0 counters = no PMU = VM tell. Raise to version>=4, gp>=4 to require a modern profile.

rapl_check.comment: With host-sensors passthrough the guest should see RAPL present and package energy increasing. Absent/zero = no passthrough (and a VM tell if the profile claims a real CPU).
